label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame
starts too bright: an attack in its envelope

R1.reason: The effect is a burst of soft round blobs fanning out from the centre, with radial streaks in frames 4 to 7. It reads as a smoke or explosion puff more than a sludge spit that splashes: there is no liquid edge, no droplets falling back, and no spit travelling before it splashes. The 'splash' is only partly carried.

R2.reason: Frames are 64 by 64 and the effect fills them as a splash should. Border measures 0.035 at most, so nothing is clipped at the edges. Each frame is the same size and the burst is centred.

R3.reason: The core glows yellow-lime (frames 2 to 4, near-white centres) and the body is a bright yellow-green. Sludge in the brief is green-grey, and this reads closer to neon yellow-green than to the murky green-grey of the pumping station. Right family, too bright and too saturated.

R4.reason: The kind of motion is right: a burst that spreads and fades to dark by frames 10 and 11, with 12 frames and the last frame at 0. Two measures are off against the explosion class. First frame is 0.82 bright where the class takes 0 to 0.22, so it starts as an attack rather than a build. Jitter is 1.68 against 1.04 to 1.48: the blob cluster reshuffles from frame to frame (visible between frames 0 and 1, and 4 and 5), so it flickers. Peak at 0.36 and border are within the class.

R5.reason: The file is named fw_spit, the brief's sprite, with type parallel and format additive, a legal GoldSrc pairing that suits a glow on black. Additive draws the dark background as nothing, which is what the frames rely on. I have no slot type from the brief to compare against, so this rests on the measured header and the name.
